title: Why Five? — The Pentagon's Spectrum
description: Interactive C_n cycle graph and its adjacency spectrum. Every eigenvalue and every rigidity claim is bound to a machine-checked theorem in the Brockian verified core; unbacked claims render BLOCKED. A picture cannot outrun its proof.

claims.claim: The eigenvalues of Cₙ are exactly the circulant modes 2·cos(2πk/n).
λ = 2 is always the largest eigenvalue of Cₙ.
The whole spectrum lies in the interval [−2, 2].
For the pentagon, 2·cos(2π/5) = φ − 1 — the golden eigenvalue.
The pentagon's second adjacency eigenvalue is −φ.
Among primes, φ − 1 lies in spec(C_p) if and only if p = 5.
The spectral field is real-quadratic (golden) iff n ∈ {5, 8, 10, 12}.
The pentagon's algebraic connectivity is λ₂(C₅) = 2 − 1/φ.
The full automorphism group of the pentagon is the dihedral group D₅.
